Mrs. Christine Low was in the sick bay to pat on her to have some sleep while Mrs. Hor and Mrs. Jasmine Ng making a trip to Xin Ling’s house to pick up medication. Mr. Yeo and Mrs. Hor have kept me updated via WhatsApp on her condition.  Not knowing that she was down with pneumonia, Xin Ling continued with her 3rd and 4th day of exam with fever running.  I would like thank and a big shout out to BLGPS especially to Mrs. Hor, Mr. Yeo, Mrs. Jasmine Ng and Mrs. Christine Low who have demonstrated the BLGPS’s value and given all the care, support to Xin Ling to help her crossing the PSLE finishing line. As a parent, this school well exceeded my expectations. Have to admit this wasn't my choice school but there was a vacancy, transfer case as we moved to the area. Firstly the uniform is brilliantly designed as no ironing is needed, the polo tee is wrinke-free. Shoes are black, no cleaning needed unless muddy which is almost never happening. Few schools have a board of directors and this has and board members have strong creed to foster good character in all students. My child turned from unruly, traumatised from previous (popular) school, scatterbrained, irresponsible, to a focused, independent, hardworking, reliable student. The school staff train all students to be independent from primary 1. By primary 2 they are already able to orientate new P1 students unsupervised (other sch use older P4 or P5 students). P1 students are taught how to write down instructions and homework just like other schools but by P3 they are already memorising what they need for the next days. Every school has enrichment courses that change yearly, normally 2 or 3 while Pei Tong offers 10-15 per year, no kidding. Bullying is not allowed and strict discipline protocol is in place that tackles the problem within 24h (other schools either don't care or procrastinate because overwhelmed with cases). Students after school are orderly, well behaved, and calm. Students of other schools are by contrast, running everywhere, unruly, swearing and screaming. You can really see the difference. Academic ability depends on the individual not the school but character building is best built from young and Pei Tong does a marvellous job. My child already graduated and is attending one of the top sec schools, scores A1 A2 in several subjects even without tuition there, doesn't take notes, everything memorised naturally in class, cool attitude no stress, thanks to training from Pei Tong, it saves us money!

as a graduate of this school (just this year!) i think i’m decently qualified to say it’s pretty good—not the best, but decent. although if you’re looking to enrol your child in a primary school and are looking at google maps reviews to do so… honestly just search on kiasuparents or something, i don’t know  anyway!  pros are that there are some decent teachers! there’s miss diane chua, trained to teach SS, EL, MA and SCI—and does so really well !! (she does put discipline very highly however, so tread carefully if you’re studying with her as a form teacher.)  extra kudos to miss yue si wei, who always puts in extra effort to make sure her students understand every little bit of her lessons—although she’s recently left alongside a few really good teachers mentioned in another review here—and miss liu xiaoyu (刘老师), who teaches either primary 4, 5 or 6 HCL classes with tools like classcraft, motivational rewards and other prizes, all to make sure you look forward and pay attention to lessons every single day.  she was the one who sparked my interest in chinese, in fact! getting into her classes isn’t easy, but the marginally more rigorous curriculum sure is worth it under her guidance.  of course, there are many other great teachers…  but there are also the less popular ones. i won’t provide any names, but there are a handful of teachers that have done rather atrocious things to their students, and others that just… don’t care. the former are mostly elderly substitute teachers, though, so here’s to hoping they go easier on the students from now on, haha.  the facilities are decently clean as well, with cleaning robots stationed in the 2 sport halls and elderly janitors helping to mop the floors and sweep the cabinets, et cetera—there’s also a treasure trove worth of drama between two of them… don’t take this an excuse to sit in the toilets and skip lessons, future students. i can’t say much about the students themselves as they do change, after all, but my experience was that they’re reasonably friendly once you hit primary 5 and 6, since at least half will have matured and found it boring to bully people (read: me. yes, i did get bullied—but i did befriend some of them in the last two years of my time at SKGPS, so that’s a plus, i guess?)  all in all, this school’s rank as the 22nd primary school with best academics is … pretty deserved, i’d say, but it all boils down to the kid and the teachers he/she/they get to meet!
